name: Stationary Split Squat
definition: A stationary unilateral-emphasis compound exercise performed from a fixed sagittal split stance. The roster owns floor-supported barbell and paired-dumbbell split squats using an approximately leg-length stance and lead thigh-parallel endpoint, plus a one-dumbbell goblet fixture with source-unreported stance length and near-right-angle lead knee. These loaded floor fixtures keep an erect torso, full lead-foot contact, and rear-forefoot floor support. It also owns two source-exact rear-foot-elevated fixtures: a high-bar setup with the rear foot fixed at patella height and a two-dumbbell setup with the top of the rear foot supported on a bench of unreported height. Each keeps its contacts fixed and returns through lead-side hip extension, knee extension, and ankle plantarflexion. Dynamic lunges, unsupported rear-foot variants, other elevations, Smith, kettlebell, and deficit branches remain outside this contract. Tibialis anterior is authored as an ankle/foot stabilizer on the stationary and rear-foot-elevated split-squat fixtures. This is a categorical anatomy-and-mechanics inference supported by measured activity in related protocols, not exact-fixture EMG or primary/secondary training emphasis. Existing geometry sources remain authoritative; machine fixtures are not added by this evidence review. TFL receives stabilizer credit for hip, pelvic and knee alignment in the asymmetric fixed stance. Collings recorded TFL in a related two-dumbbell split squat; its modeled gluteal outcomes do not establish TFL force or ranking. Transfer to exact barbell, floor-supported and rear-foot-elevated fixtures is categorical anatomy and mechanics. Rear support, stance, load placement and depth retain their own source boundaries; no hip-extension or dynamic hip-flexion role is added. The unloaded floor and Bulgarian bench fixtures share this stationary split-stance family. Hands stay on the hips, no implement-grip roles are credited, and resistance remains unquantified rather than assigning a bodyweight percentage. Floor geometry transfers categorically from reviewed split-squat standards and explicit unloaded warmups; the unloaded bench posture follows NASM. Bench height and stance length remain unreported for both top-of-foot bench fixtures. The Boxing Science goblet branch holds one dumbbell at the chest in a fixed floor split stance, descends to a front-leg right angle, and returns without stepping; its stance length is not prescribed. This one-implement branch does not inherit the paired-dumbbell load or Song depth prescription.

execution.startingPosition: Place a barbell securely across your upper back and hold it with both palms facing forward. Take a split stance about as long as the distance from the outside of your hip to the outside of your ankle, with your front foot flat and the ball of your rear foot on the floor.
execution.movement: Lower until your lead thigh is approximately parallel to the floor.
execution.endpoint: Stop when your lead thigh is approximately parallel to the floor.
execution.returnPhase: Push through your front foot and straighten the front hip and knee to rise back to the split stance. Finish in the same split stance without stepping between repetitions.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep that stance length throughout the set, using a comfortable position for each foot. Keep both foot contacts fixed.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your torso erect with the bar held securely across your upper back.
disqualifyingCompensations: Stepping between repetitions turns the split squat into a lunge.
Leaning the torso forward turns the split squat into a hinge.
Shortening the stance turns the split squat into a narrow squat.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete every repetition with one leg forward, then switch to the other leg.

execution.startingPosition: Log one dumbbell's weight, not the pair total. Hold one matching dumbbell at each side and take a fixed split stance about as long as the distance from the outside of your hip to the outside of your ankle. Keep the lead foot flat and the rear forefoot on the floor.
execution.movement: Keep both foot contacts fixed and lower with an erect torso until the lead thigh is approximately parallel to the floor.
execution.endpoint: Stop at lead-thigh-parallel depth without shortening the stance or moving either foot.
execution.returnPhase: Push through the lead foot and extend the lead hip, knee, and ankle to return to the same split stance.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the lead knee tracking with the foot and both dumbbells hanging neutrally at your sides.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the torso erect and use no rear-foot elevation or external support.
disqualifyingCompensations: Stepping between repetitions turns the movement into a lunge.
Elevating the rear foot turns it into a rear-foot-elevated split squat.
Holding one dumbbell or moving the pair away from the sides changes the reviewed load geometry.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete all repetitions with one lead leg, then repeat with the other leg.

execution.startingPosition: Set a stable rear box to the bottom-of-kneecap height, secure the rear foot against its posterior stop, place the lead leg in line with that hip, and hold the bar high on the upper back.
execution.movement: Lower with both contacts fixed until the lead knee reaches approximately ninety degrees and the kneecap is aligned over the lead toe.
execution.endpoint: Reach the individualized reviewed depth without changing the foot positions or rear support.
execution.returnPhase: Rise through the lead hip, knee, and ankle without stepping between repetitions.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the lead knee tracking with the foot and do not let the rear foot slide.
execution.supportAndPosture: Maintain the high-bar position while the unreported trunk angle remains consistent across the set.
disqualifyingCompensations: Losing or sliding the rear-foot support changes the reviewed fixture.
Stepping or drifting from the individualized stance changes the stationary split squat.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the set with one lead leg, then repeat with the other leg leading.

execution.startingPosition: Log one dumbbell's weight, not the pair total. Hold one matching dumbbell at each side, place the lead foot fully on the floor, and rest the top of the rear foot on a stable bench. The source did not report a bench height or numeric stance length.
execution.movement: Lower with both foot contacts fixed until the lead thigh is approximately parallel to the floor.
execution.endpoint: Reach lead-thigh-parallel depth without shifting the feet or lifting the rear foot from the bench.
execution.returnPhase: Push through the lead foot and extend the lead hip, knee, and ankle to return to the same split stance.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the lead knee tracking with the foot and both dumbbells moving together at your sides.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the torso braced and use the bench only to support the top of the rear foot.
disqualifyingCompensations: Stepping between repetitions turns the movement into a lunge.
Pushing deliberately through the rear foot changes the lead-leg fixture.
Using a barbell or holding the dumbbells away from the sides changes the reviewed load placement.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete all repetitions with one lead leg, then repeat with the other leg.

execution.startingPosition: Take a fixed split stance about one leg-length long, with the lead foot flat and the rear forefoot on the floor. Place both hands on your hips and use no external weight.
execution.movement: Bend the lead hip and knee to lower until the lead thigh is approximately parallel to the floor.
execution.endpoint: Reach lead-thigh-parallel depth with both foot contacts unchanged.
execution.returnPhase: Push through the lead foot to extend the hip, knee and ankle and rise in the same stance.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the lead knee tracking with the foot and avoid rotating the pelvis.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the torso erect and braced, with both hands resting on the hips.
disqualifyingCompensations: Stepping between repetitions changes the stationary exercise into a lunge.
Using external weight or hand support changes the unloaded fixture.
Jumping or lifting either support contact changes the reviewed motion.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the set with one leg leading, then repeat with the other leg.

execution.startingPosition: Stand facing away from a stable bench. Rest the top of the rear foot on it and place the lead foot flat on the floor. Place both hands on your hips and use no external weight.
execution.movement: Bend the lead hip and knee to lower until the lead thigh is approximately parallel to the floor.
execution.endpoint: Reach lead-thigh-parallel depth with both foot contacts unchanged.
execution.returnPhase: Push through the lead foot to extend the hip, knee and ankle and rise in the same stance.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the lead knee tracking with the foot and avoid rotating the pelvis.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the torso erect and braced, with both hands resting on the hips.
disqualifyingCompensations: Stepping between repetitions changes the stationary exercise into a lunge.
Using external weight or hand support changes the unloaded fixture.
Jumping or lifting either support contact changes the reviewed motion.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the set with one leg leading, then repeat with the other leg.

execution.startingPosition: Hold one dumbbell vertically with both hands at the chest; log the entire dumbbell weight. Set a fixed split stance with the lead foot flat and rear forefoot on the floor.
execution.movement: Keep both feet in place, trunk upright, and lower straight down.
execution.endpoint: Stop with the front leg about a right angle and the rear knee behind the hips.
execution.returnPhase: Drive through the lead foot to rise into the same split stance without stepping.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the dumbbell close to the chest and control the lead knee and pelvis over the planted foot.
execution.supportAndPosture: Maintain full lead-foot and rear-forefoot contact without a bench or hand support.
disqualifyingCompensations: Stepping between repetitions changes this stationary split squat into a lunge.
Moving the dumbbell to one hand or both sides changes the reviewed goblet load placement.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the set with one lead leg, then switch legs.
